text: Write a story which begins with the following sentence: He had only one more chance to succeed,
and he knew it. In your writing, create a sense of suspense and anticipation.
Write two contrasting pieces (300–450 words each), the first about a tourist resort at its busiest
time of year, and the second about the same resort when it is much less busy. In your writing,
create a sense of atmosphere and place.
Write a descriptive piece called Backstage, about the activities going on behind the scenes while
a play is on at a theatre. In your writing, focus on sounds, light and movements to help your reader
imagine the scene.
Section B: Writing for an audience
You have been asked to give a speech called Technology in Schools to a large group of students
at your school. Write the text for the speech. In your writing, create a sense of enthusiasm about
how technology may change schools in the future.
A national newspaper recently published an article called The Right to Vote at 16? Write two letters
(300–450 words each) to the editor of the newspaper, one supporting the right to vote at 16, and
the other challenging it. In your writing, create a sense of opposing views.
Write the script of a voiceover for a TV news report of a sporting event. The script should cover the
outcome of the event, and some discussion of it. In your writing, create a sense of excitement and
interest.
